classification models trained on artificial imagery with added simulated image degradatios are able to predict image quality of real camera imagery.

the development of a novel approach to image quality metrics, which can be applied to a variety of camera settings and image degradations.
the investigation of a novel method for image quality assessment of imagers by classification of geometric primitive patterns.

the development of a novel approach to image quality evaluation of camera imagers by comparison of classification results of models individually trained on simple classification tasks on geometric primitives.

the approach of this paper can be considered as an alternative to existing image quality metrics, which are typically not applicable to real camera data, or to subjective quality assessments, which are expensive and not always reproducible.
the proposed approach can serve as a valuable tool for image quality evaluation of imagers and camera systems.
the presented approach has the potential to be a powerful method to image quality assessment.

the presented approach allows for a task dependent evaluation of image quality for a large variety of imaging devices and applications, which is a major advantage over other image quality metrics.

the proposed approach allows for the assessment of image quality in terms of task specific performance for real camera images.
